sentences.english_text: A little girl, playing in the park, happened to look up, and saw Drippy.
And it looked as though a tear had fallen from the eye of the saint.
The little girl's mouth fell open in amazement.
Look, Mother!
The statue is crying!
Don't be silly.
Statues can't cry.
But it is!
That's ridiculous.
Her mother scolded, and she looked up, and her mouth fell open.
The statue did seem to be crying.
She called her husband over.
Henry, I think the statue of the saint is crying.
Her husband said, Really, Martha, don't be so silly.
Statues can't cry.
But he looked up, and his mouth fell open.
That statue is crying!
It's a miracle!
A woman standing next to him said, What's a miracle?
The man pointed to Drippy, who was unaware that he looked just like a tear.
By now, a crowd had begun to gather.
What's happening?
A miracle has happened!
The statue of the saint is crying!
And everyone looked up at Drippy, and they said, It's a tear!
The saint is crying!
And pretty soon, the crowd had grown to hundreds of people.
And as the word spread, more people kept arriving from everywhere, and they filled the square, all of them looking up and pointing at Drippy.
The saint is crying!
The saint is crying!
Drippy watched the people in the park below, and he heard all the yelling, but he could not understand what they were saying.
They seemed to be very excited about the statue he was on.
Maybe it's some kind of special statue.
He had no idea that he was the reason for all the excitement.
That they thought he was the tear the statue was shedding.
I wonder how I'm going to get down from here.
Perhaps my pigeon friend will come and fly me down.
Then I can get back on the park bench, and the wind will never know that I broke my promise.
Of course, Drippy did not know that the wind already knew that he had broken his promise.
But no pigeons came to Drippy's rescue.
They were frightened by the hundreds of people standing in the square, pointing at the statue and yelling.
